        proc_time <- difftime(Sys.time(), .start_time, units = "secs")
        proc_time <- round(as.numeric(proc_time), 2)

        mins <- proc_time %/% 60
        secs <- proc_time %% 60

        proc_time <- if (mins > 0) {
          sprintf("%dm %.1fs", mins, secs)
        } else {
          sprintf("%.1fs", secs)
        }

        sprintf(
          "<p class='chunk-timing'>%s</p>",
          paste0("Code execution time: ", proc_time)
        )
      }
    }
  })
)

## Introduction

**Goal:** Optimize the NetC14 hyperparameter $\gamma$ - the weight on the
precision penalty - with respect to the held-out likelihood of radiocarbon
samples. Because this criterion uses only the observed samples, it can also be
computed on real data where the true ages and density are unknown. The sparsemax
temperature $\pi$ is fixed at 1, since it overlaps with $\gamma$ in promoting
sparsity, and tuning both leaves the optimum poorly identified.

**Data:** For model tuning, data are simulated according to the generative
model.

**Method:** We sweep a fixed grid of $\gamma$ values against a fixed panel of
simulated chronologies, scoring every value against the same set of
chronologies to focus on variance across values. Samples in
each chronology are split into five folds. Each configuration is fit to four
folds and scored by the log marginal likelihood of the fifth, rotating through
all five.

## Data

```{r}
#| label: intcal20
intcal20 <- structure(
  read.csv("data/intcal20.csv"),
  class = c("Calibration", "data.frame"),
  curve = "IntCal20"
)

intcal20 <- transform(intcal20, f14c_mu = exp(-c14_age / LIBBY))
intcal20 <- transform(intcal20, f14c_sigma = f14c_mu * c14_error / LIBBY)
```

The chronology grid crosses problem size, sample count, mixture complexity, and
component distribution scenarios. Every value of $\gamma$ is evaluated against
every chronological scenario.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-grid
gammas <- seq(1, 7, by = 0.5)

evaluation_grid <- expand.grid(
  n_years = c(500, 2500, 12500) - 1,
  n_samples = c(50, 250, 1250),
  n_clusters = c(1, 3, 9),
  distribution = c("gaussian", "uniform", "skewed"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

n_scenarios <- nrow(evaluation_grid)
```

## Tuning

To make this loop as efficient as possible, we precompute the chronologies and
draw samples from them. Each chronology is simulated **once** and reused across 
all configurations. 

```{r}
#| label: simulation-loop
#| output: false
#| time_it: true
simulations <- vector("list", n_scenarios)

for (i in seq_len(n_scenarios)) {
  set.seed(STARGATE + i)

  # scenario
  n_years <- evaluation_grid[["n_years"]][i]
  n_clusters <- evaluation_grid[["n_clusters"]][i]
  n_samples <- evaluation_grid[["n_samples"]][i]
  distribution <- evaluation_grid[["distribution"]][i]
  start <- sample(seq(100, 49500 - n_years), 1)
  end <- start + n_years

  # simulate chronology and draw samples
  chronology <- simulate_chronology(start, end, n_clusters, distribution)
  samples <- sample_dates(chronology, n_samples, intcal20)

  # k-fold
  folds <- split(seq_len(n_samples), sample(rep_len(1:5, n_samples)))

  simulations[[i]] <- lapply(gammas, \(gamma) {
    list(
      id = i,
      start = start,
      gamma = gamma,
      samples = samples,
      folds = folds
    )
  })
}

simulations <- do.call(c, simulations)
```

The configuration sweep only has to fit NetC14 and evaluate against each hold 
out.

```{r}
#| label: tuning-loop
#| output: false
#| time_it: true
clusters <- makeCluster(14)

fns <- c(
  "calibrate.R",
  "constants.R",
  "dataframe-helpers.R",
  "mixture-helpers.R",
  "netc14.R",
  "sample-dates.R",
  "simulate-chronology.R",
  "spd.R"
)

clusterExport(
  clusters,
  varlist = c(
    "fns",
    "intcal20"
  ),
  envir = environment()
)

clusterEvalQ(clusters, {
  library(torch)
  torch_set_num_threads(1)
  lapply(file.path("R", fns), source, verbose = FALSE)
})

tuning_results <- parLapplyLB(
  clusters,
  simulations,
  \(scenario) {
    gamma <- scenario[["gamma"]]

    calibrated_dates <- with(scenario, calibrate(samples, intcal20))

    heldout <- 0

    for (fold in scenario[["folds"]]) {
      training_dates <- structure(
        calibrated_dates[-fold, ],
        class = class(calibrated_dates),
        start = attr(calibrated_dates, "start"),
        end = attr(calibrated_dates, "end")
      )
      netc_cv <- netc(training_dates, gamma = gamma, pi = 1)
      ll <- logLik(netc_cv, calibrated_dates[fold, , drop = FALSE])
      heldout <- heldout + ll
    }

    data.frame(
      scenario = scenario[["id"]],
      start = scenario[["start"]],
      gamma = gamma,
      nll = -sum(heldout) / nrow(calibrated_dates)
    )
  },
  chunk.size = 1
)

stopCluster(clusters)
tuning_results <- do.call(rbind, tuning_results)
```

Combine results and save.

```{r}
#| label: save-results
evaluation_grid[["scenario"]] <- seq_len(n_scenarios)
tuning_results <- merge(tuning_results, evaluation_grid, all.x = TRUE)

tuning_results <- tuning_results[c(
  "scenario",
  "gamma",
  "n_years",
  "n_samples",
  "n_clusters",
  "distribution",
  "start",
  "nll"
)]

write.csv(
  tuning_results,
  file = "data/tuning-results.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

## Results

Held-out NLL is normalized within each scenario as the difference from the best
configuration for that scenario, so scenarios with different sample sizes and
intervals are comparable.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-results
tuning_results <- transform(
  tuning_results,
  nll = nll - ave(nll, scenario, FUN = min)
)

tuning_results <- aggregate(
  nll ~ gamma,
  data = tuning_results,
  FUN = \(.x) quantile(.x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
)

tuning_results <- do.call(data.frame, tuning_results)
names(tuning_results) <- c("gamma", "lower", "median", "upper")

best <- tuning_results[which.min(tuning_results[["median"]]), ]
```

```{r}
#| label: visualize-tuning-results
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
svglite(
  "figures/tuning-objectives.svg",
  width = 5.5,
  height = 3
)

par(defaults)
par(mai = c(0.6, 0.6, 0, 0))

with(tuning_results, new_plot(range(gamma), range(lower, upper)))
add_grid()

with(
  tuning_results,
  segments(gamma, lower, gamma, upper, col = coolors("gray"))
)

with(tuning_results, points(gamma, median, pch = 19, col = coolors("gray")))

with(best, points(gamma, median, pch = 19, col = coolors("orange"), cex = 1.5))

x_axis()
y_axis()

x_title("PRECISION PENALTY [γ]")
y_title("HELD-OUT NLL [Δ]")

dev.off()
```

### Optimal configuration

The optimal $\gamma$ minimizes the median held-out NLL across scenarios. It is
highlighted in orange in the figure above, with whiskers spanning the
interquartile range.

```{r}
#| label: best-configuration
best
```
